findings.title: SoA layout, profile-as-data, and force accumulation match architecture principles
findings.description: The design directly implements the architecture's principles: data-oriented SoA agent state (`AgentState` with separate arrays), forces-not-decisions (force protocols summing force vectors), profile as a dataclass with no silent defaults, pluggable spatial queries via `Protocol`, and a `BulkForce` interface structurally identical to a GPU dispatch. The 2D `DIMS` constant and `float64` internal precision with Float32 deferred to the serialization boundary correctly thread the architecture's "define internal precision, defer conversion" guidance.

findings.title: Subset-evaluable tick and full-population neighbor visibility match multi-resolution requirement
findings.description: The design correctly implements the architecture's subset-evaluable tick principle: `active_indices` parameter on `tick()`, spatial index built from the full population, and inactive agents remaining visible as neighbors to active agents. This is exactly the interface the architecture specifies as the engine's contribution to the world server's multi-resolution simulation strategy, without the engine taking on scaling decisions itself.

findings.title: Tick determinism, fixed timestep, and semi-implicit Euler match architecture guidance
findings.description: The design uses fixed-timestep integration and semi-implicit Euler (explicitly named as a stability improvement over standard Euler in the architecture's Technical Considerations). The verification walkthrough includes a determinism check that matches the architecture's "given the same state and inputs, a tick produces the same outputs" requirement.

findings.title: Scope boundaries correctly defer non-foundation concerns
findings.description: The "Excluded" list correctly places spatial hash optimization in slice 105, behavioral forces (cohesion/separation/alignment) in slice 101, persistence/serialization/networking with the world server, and visualization/rendering outside the engine. The environment-layer interface, mentioned as an architectural principle ("Environment as input surface"), is appropriately deferred — the architecture places environment under its own future initiative and slice 100 establishes only the engine's behavioral core.

findings.title: Failure modes and error handling align with project guidelines
findings.description: The design explicitly states `BehavioralProfile` fields have no default values and fail explicitly on missing fields (matching the "Never use silent fallback values" project principle). The slice does not introduce new I/O paths or external message types that would require explicit failure-mode handling beyond the deterministic in-process tick — the spatial query and force protocols operate on arrays in-process, so the standard hung/disconnect failure modes from external I/O do not apply here. The deterministic-output requirement eliminates the ambiguous "peer disconnect mid-send" concern.

findings.title: Proportional scope for a 3/5-effort foundation slice
findings.description: The design's mechanism count (AgentState container, BehavioralProfile dataclass, two force protocols, one spatial protocol, one integration function, one tick function) is proportional to the slice's foundation role. Brute-force spatial query is explicitly accepted as O(n²) at hundreds-of-agents scale; no premature optimization is included. The verification walkthrough exercises determinism, motion-under-force, and subset evaluation without over-specifying. No section restates other documents; no abstraction exists that nothing uses yet; no heavier mechanism is chosen where a lighter one meets the requirement.
